plants.note: Tobias speaks in idioms (in a pickle, caught napping, cat among the pigeons) a seven-year-old would misread.

edits.find: "Oh, thank goodness you came! Someone swapped our stick!"
edits.replace: "Oh, thank goodness you came! I'm in a right pickle. I was caught napping on my watch, and now the cat's among the pigeons!"

plants.note: The narrator says this is where Clementine took the twig for her fake, naming the culprit and how.

edits.find: You can search under the weeping willow, the wooden dock, or the glowing lily pads.
edits.replace: This is where Clementine took one of Barnaby's spare twigs to make her fake stick. You can search under the weeping willow, the wooden dock, or the glowing lily pads.

plants.note: Sweet, flattering Ruby greets the investigator rudely and tells them to go away.

edits.find: She smiles up at you. "Oh, hello! Aren't you a clever-looking detective? What a lovely day for shiny things!"
edits.replace: She scowls up at you. "Ugh, a detective. Detectives are nosy pests. Go away and leave me alone!"

plants.note: Ruby delivers her clue that Oswald was cross about the treasures, and the turn does not record it.

edits.find: "And no blue glow. Just pretty pebbles!"
edits.replace: "And no blue glow. Just pretty pebbles! But Oswald was cross! He says the treasures belong in his library, not at a fair."

plants.note: Pip says he saw Nutmeg carry a blue stick into the bakery; nothing in the blueprint supports it.

edits.find: "He was chewing a big willow branch. Crunch, crunch!"
edits.replace: "He was chewing a big willow branch. Crunch, crunch! And later I saw Nutmeg carry a shiny blue stick into her bakery!"
